original_question: Give concrete examples of weak biquandles that are not strong.
target_in_paper: Section 8.1, Problem 10 (“The fundamental biquandle”), specifically the adjacent subquestion “Are there good examples of weak biquandles which are not strong?”; the meaning of “strong” is supplied earlier in Definition 5.1 of §5.1. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly isolates the paper’s auxiliary example-existence question about separating weak from strong biquandles, rather than the broader surrounding question of whether the fundamental biquandle classifies virtual links up to mirror images. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
missing_details: The paper does not formally state a separate definition of “weak biquandle”; instead, Definition 5.1 gives the base notion of biquandle, and “strong” is the extra requirement that the elements x, y, z, t required in axiom (3) be uniquely determined. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

To be stand-alone, the question should say that the requested example must satisfy all of Definition 5.1, not merely fail strongness. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

The failure of strongness should be quantified precisely: for at least one pair a, b in the biquandle, the axiom-(3) witnesses are not unique. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

This is not a separately numbered open problem but a side question immediately after Problem 10 in §8.1, so that location should be named if one wants the paper-faithful target. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

No ambient ring, field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency restrictions are part of this problem; the hidden structure consists instead of the four binary operations and the existence/uniqueness clauses in Definition 5.1. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

The paper itself notes that this example-existence problem is already solved in [220], so the draft omits that historical status. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
refined_question: Exhibit an explicit biquandle B in the sense of Definition 5.1 of §5.1—that is, a set with the four biquandle operations satisfying the axioms of Definition 5.1—such that B is not strong: for some pair a, b in B, the elements x, y, z, t whose existence is required in axiom (3) are not uniquely determined. This is the paper’s side question asking for a good example of a weak biquandle that is not strong. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
justification: This is the closest official formulation in the paper: the exact example-existence question appears immediately under Problem 10 in §8.1, while the only nearby place that makes “strong” precise is Definition 5.1 in §5.1, where strongness is the uniqueness of the axiom-(3) witnesses x, y, z, t. Because the paper also says “This problem is solved in [220],” the refined version should preserve the narrow example/existence focus of the original sentence and should not be broadened into the larger mirror-classification question for the fundamental biquandle. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
